Copper Market Review 2011 and Outlook 2012 
Copper prices review in 2011 
The copper price bottomed at US$6,635/t on Oct. 3, the lowest level in 2011, and it 
fluctuated between US$7,000-9,000/t within the year. The Eurozone debt crisis and the 
slowdown of China’s economy growth are the two key factors which can affect the metal 
market in 2011.  
The average copper price of cash month and 3-month dropped to US$7,488/t and 
US$7,510/t in Q4 2011, decreasing by 16.72% and 16.66% on a quarterly basis and declining 
by 13.29% and 12.85% on a yearly basis.  
But as the prices were higher in the first half compared with the corresponding period of 
the previous year, the annual average price was still above the level in 2010. The average 
copper price of cash month and 3-month dropped to US$8,820/t and US$8,834/t in 2011, 
decreasing by 17.07% and 17.01% both on a yearly basis.

Smelting/refining capacity continues expanding 
  According to data from Antaike, by the end of 2011, Chinese newly added smelting and 
refining capacity was 600kt/y and 1.15Mt/y, and Chinese total smelting and refining capacity 
reached 4.07Mt/y and 7.13Mt/y respectively. 
  The newly added smelting and refining capacity were much higher than that in 2010, which 
was another new expanding period for Chinese copper smelting/refining capacity. It is 
estimated that this kind of expanding situation will continue until 2013 and newly added 
smelting and refining capacity will exceed 600kt/y and 1Mt/y. 
  Such kind of expansion for Chinese smelting and refining capacity has become key drivers 
for domestic refined copper growth and important factor that depressed TC/RCs. 
Copper- in-concentrate supply in a small shortage 
  According to data from China Nonferrous metals Industry Association (CNIA), domestic 
copper-in-concentrate output during Jan to Nov 2011 was 1.14Mt, up by 9.3% y/y. Antaike 
estimates that total copper-in-concentrate output in 2011 will reach 1.23Mt, up by 7.9% y/y. 
Import volume in 2011 basically kept flat with that in 2010, at 1745kt. Copper-in-concentrate 
demand increased by 12.1% to 2933kt in 2011. Domestic supply shortage was 63kt in 2011. 
Antaike estimates that copper-in-concentrate output in 2012 will keep rapid growth trend 
and import will return to growth. So it is possible for copper-in-concentrate supply to increase 
in 2012. But copper-in-concentrate demand will have a faster growth due to a new expanding 
round for Chinese copper smelting/refining capacity since 2011. Antaike estimates that 
copper-in-concentrate supply will still be in shortage in 2012 and the shortage will reach 
about 100kt.

Domestic secondary copper supply in surplus 
  As the abolition of tax rebate for copper scraps, copper scraps prices have been losing its 
price advantage and began to be higher than refined copper prices after September 2011, 
which caused partial copper semis enterprises who use copper scraps as major raw materials 
in shutdown or in half shutdown. 
  According to data from CNIA, Chinese secondary copper output was 1.73Mt in 2010, up 
by 25.2% y/y, accounting for 37.8% of total refined copper output, 4.2 percentage points 
higher than 2009. During Jan to Nov, domestic secondary copper output was 1.67Mt, a rise of 
3.8% y/y, 20 percentage points lower than the same period of 2010, about 35.1% of the total 
refined copper output during this period. Decline of growth rate and proportion reflected the 
influence on domestic secondary copper production by above mentioned factors from one 
side. 
  Copper scraps import was 4.24Mt (physical quantity) during Jan to Nov, up by 7.09% y/y. 
According to Antaike’s investigation, downstream enterprises had other channels to get 
copper scraps. On the whole, copper scraps market was in surplus, at about 60kt, and the 
surplus mainly appeared in H2 2011. 
  
Refined copper output increases rapidly, but consumption down 
According to data from State Statistics Bureau, domestic refined copper output during Jan 
to Nov was about 4.78Mt, up by 16.3% y/y. Data released by CNIA showed that refined 
copper output was 4.75Mt, up by 13.4% y/y. Calculated by above growth trend, refined 
copper output will reach 5.20Mt in 2011. 
  Antaike has different idea from above institutions’. According to Antaike’s data, Chinese 
12 refined copper enterprises whose refined copper output accounted for about 70% of the 
national total produced 3.52Mt refined copper during Jan to Nov 2011, up by 14% y/y. 
Antaike estimates that domestic refined copper output will be about 5.18Mt in 2011.  
  In respect of refined copper consumption, electric power industry and air conditioning and 
refrigeration industry made great contribution on the growth of copper consumption. Rural 
network reconstruction in 2011 raised investment in this industry, whose driving force for 
copper consumption was obvious. Benefited by such home appliances promotion policies, as 
Home Appliances to the Countryside, Traded in and Energy subsidies. Air conditioning and 
refrigeration industry had a rapid growth in 2011. As the implement of China’s real estate 
regulatory policy in 2011, total investment in real estate and new commenced area had a 
decline in growth, which is unfavorable for Chinese copper consumption. Growth rate 
slowdown of China’s autos, reduced investment in railway fundamental construction and less 
order forms in ship building industry gave great pressures on copper consumption in 2011 
after continuous two year’s high growth in Chinese transportation industry. Electronics 
industry has a stable development in recent years. 
  Data released by the NBS showed that copper semis output was 981kt in Nov, up by 7% 
m/m. Antaike estimates that copper semis consumption will be suppressed at a relative degree 
because most of enterprises will make more attention to accounts recovery and claiming the 
debt at year end. 
  According to statistic from China Electricity Council, total investment in electric power 
construction reached 620.7 bln yuan during Jan to Nov, up by 9.5% y-o-y. Of which 
investment in power source and power grid were 309.3 bln yuan and 311.4 bln yuan, up by 
0.5% y-o-y and 20.1% y-o-y. This year investment in power grid kept a continuous rise while 
growth rate of investment in power source slowed down. Of investment in power source, 
investment in hydropower, nuclear power and wind power were respectively 78.2 bln yuan, 
65.6 bln yuan and 64.2 bln yuan, which accounted for 67.3% of the total investment in power 
source, 3.9 percentage points higher than last year. Share of investment in thermal power was 
only 29.6%, 6.5 percentage points lower than last year. 
  Antaike estimates that domestic refined copper consumption will reach 7.33Mt, up by 7.8% 
y/y, 4 percentage points lower than last year.

Refined copper import shows a low-high trend, but export a high-low 
trend 
  Chinese refined copper import had a decline in H1 2011 but export increased rapidly due to 
higher international refined copper prices than domestic prices and high level of domestic 
refined copper inventory. The situation was reversed in H2 2011. Refined copper export had a 
continuous growth and export declined apparently with the growth of restocking need. 
 
Chart 3 Chinese Refined Copper Monthly Import (t)  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Data released by the Customs showed that refined copper import during Jan to Nov was 
2.43Mt, down by 9.8% y/y. Refined copper import in Nov reached 344kt, the second after the 
highest level set in June 2009, at 379kt. Restocking need appeared in H2 211, rapid growth of 
yuan appreciation, decline of refined copper output in Q4 and financial requirements are the 
main factors resulting in the low-high trend of Chinese refined copper import. 
  Refined copper export showed a high-low trend. Domestic refined copper export was 156kt 
during Jan to Nov, greatly up by 452.9% y/y. Refined copper export reached 147kt in H1 2011, 
up by 712.1% y/y, mainly due to lower domestic copper prices against international copper 
prices and destocking actions in domestic copper market.

Domestic refined copper supply still in surplus 
  Chinese refined copper consumption kept a continuous growth, but output had been in a 
rapid growth. High inventory caused by expanding copper smelting/refining capacity and 
high level of refined copper import caused by financing need pushed Chinese import for 
refined copper. All of above caused refined copper supply was in surplus in recent years. But 
with the growth of copper consumption, the surplus amount has been declining.

Economy Trend 
Global economy has not continued its recovery, but get into a new trouble especially 
in H2 2011. Economy trend is still an import factor which affects copper market. Debt 
problem in Euro Zone, China’s inflation and tight monetary policy, and various stimulus 
economic policies in USA, all these make great influence on the market. 
Indonesia Grasberg mine workers ended strike after Freeport bosses agreed to an increase 
in wages. Strikes happened in foreign mines increased worries about copper concentrate 
supply, which formed support for copper prices. 
Copper inventory on LME declined to about 370kt at the end of 2011, with a drop of about 
108kt compared to 478kt on Jun 10, hitting the highest level in 2011. Cancelled warrants was 
in a high level, with the highest of over 60kt, at 44kt at the end of 2011, accounting for about 
12% of inventory, a sign of continuous decline of inventory. Most of cancelled warrants came 
from warehouses in Korea and Singapore, indicating that these copper were shipped to China, 
caused by restocking need in China. 
Inventory on SHFE fell below 100kt after Oct, even below 60kt at the end of Nov. After 
that, inventory has a rise due to importing large number of refined copper. Inventory on SHFE 
maintained below 100kt.

Market Balance and Price Outlook  
Supply/demand 
 
  Antaike estimates that Chinese copper smelting and refining capacity will reach 4.72Mt 
and 8.23Mt in 2012, with newly added copper smelting and refining capacity of 650kt and 
1.1Mt. 
  Chinese copper concentrate production will keep a moderate growth in 2012. Chinese 
refined copper production is expected to keep a rapid growth as the rising supply of foreign 
raw material and domestic expanding copper capacity. It is estimated that refined copper 
production will reach 5.70Mt in 2012, with a growth rate of about 11%. 
  According to the annual central economic work conference that closed on Dec 14, the main 
theme of next year's economic and social development will be making progress while 
maintaining stability. China's current economy remains good, but the domestic and 
international environment is extremely complicated. 
In 2012, the growth rate in most of copper using industries, such as air conditioning and 
refrigeration industry, housing industry, transportation industry and etc. will be lower than 
2011. Domestic refined copper consumption in 2012 will reach 7.76Mt, up by below 6% 
against 2011. The growth rate will continue to drop.  
  Refined copper import will have a continuous decline, but in a relative high level. It is 
difficult for Chinese refined copper in 2012 to recur large amount of export.

Price Outlook in 2011 
  Macroeconomic picture is extremely unclear, which will maintain weak at least in H1 2012. 
It is difficult for global copper prices to have a unilateral rise in 2012. At the same time, 
global copper supply is still tight, which will form a support for copper price. 
  It is expected that copper price will fluctuate at a high level in whole 2012, but there exist 
many uncertainties in H1 2012.  
  In 2012 copper price on LME will keep a low-high trend, at an average price of US$ 8,000. 
Copper price on SHFE will be within a range of 45,000-70,000yuan/t, with the average price 
of 58,000yuan/t in 2012.
